description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Netic builds AI products for essential service businesses. Its Gap Year Software Engineers join the product team for 12 months to develop and deliver full-stack features for its AI platform, working directly with customers to turn their needs into reliable products.
Software Engineer building full-stack features for an agentic AI platform, delivering APIs and interfaces through production.

Responsibilities:
• Build agentic products: Design, code, and ship full-stack features for Netic’s AI platform
• Co‑create with customers: Work closely with our customers, including on-site, to understand workflows, gather feedback, and turn pain points into features that stick
• Own end‑to‑end delivery: Drive projects from spec to production, handling data models, APIs, front‑end polish, and post‑launch iteration
• Ensure quality: Build, test, and monitor features in production to ensure reliability and performance
• Learn how a company is built: Sit in on sales calls and leadership meetings to see how a fast-growing startup wins customers, makes decisions, and builds a team
• Build your founder network: Get to know our board, investors, and leaders across tech—people who can advise you, back you, or build with you when you start your own company

Requirements:
• We hire on a rolling basis, and start dates are flexible
• You've shipped real projects end-to-end, whether through school, internships, hackathons, or on your own
• Comfortable with React, TypeScript, and Python, or ready to pick them up fast
• You care about the people who use what you build and want to work with them directly
• Able to explain technical trade-offs to engineers and product decisions to customers
• You must be currently enrolled as an undergraduate at a US university and able to arrange at least one full year off from school on your own (for example, through your school's leave of absence process) before returning to finish your degree

Preferred:
• Hands‑on with LLM APIs, embeddings, or RAG patterns—or hunger to learn fast
• You want to start a company one day and want to learn how great companies are built first
